newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mostly down but jet premium edges uP.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mostly down but jet premium edges uP.

text.p: European oil swaps mostly fell on Thursday, undermined by weaker oil futures and sluggish demand for oil products.
Gasoline sunk $2 a tonne, fuel fell $1 but Brent crude CFDs were flat and jet prmeiums nudged higher.
Gasoline fell another $2 a tonne for May swaps with offers at $193 at $190.50 for June. Physical barges traded at $188.50 and $193 for loading 1-15 May.
Gasoline crack spreads against Brent were little changed with June at $4.95 a barrel and the third and fourth quarters were pegged around $4.10 and $3.10 respectively.
Gas oil against Brent remained well bid but levels were little changed from Tuesday at $4.35 a barrel on the third quarter and $4.85 on the fourth.

Jet premiums firmed 50 cents to trade at $24.50 a tonne above the IPE for May but forward periods were little changed with the third and fourth quarters holding at $27.25 and $32 above the screen respectively.
Heavy fuel dropped $1 a tonne to $81 for May barges and $86 for low sulphur. The Mediterranean traded actively between $74 and $75 for May and at $75.50 for June.

Dealers said the market remained depressed in Europe with only minimal demand from power companies and shipowners. But they also saw support from Asia where swaps edged up 41 a tonne to over $98 for May.
Brent CFDs were little changed with next week slipping a couple of cents but the week after a similar amount higher.
Next week traded at 59 cents under June but then fell back to 61 cents under with the following week around 54 cents under and the following two weeks 48 cents and 43 cents under respectively.
Wet Brent was steady in what dealers said was a slow market for North Sea crudes. -- Sam Arnold-Forster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4984
